newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria is hopeful about Sierra Leone talks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria is hopeful about Sierra Leone talks.

text.p: Envoys from Sierra Leone's military junta met West African foreign ministers on Thursday and regional power broker Nigeria said it was hopeful of progress towards resolving a standoff over their May 25 coup.

Nigeria's foreign minister, whose country heads a West African force trying to restore peace and democracy to both Sierra Leone and neighbouring Liberia, said it was looking for a speedy resolution to the crisis.
"Peace in Liberia will not be long-lasting if there is not peace in Sierra Leone," Tom Ikimi told the meeting in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan.

"We feel we have made substantial progress and that the atmosphere exists for a substantial breakthrough," he said later. He described the atmosphere at the talks as "very friendly, cordial and brotherly."

With Liberia holding national elections on Saturday to end seven years of civil war, Ikimi said Nigeria's military leader Sani Abacha, chairman of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), wanted a speedy settlement for Sierra Leone.
The junta's team was less optimistic before the talks, which Ivorian officials said would resume on Friday.

Corporal Tamba Gborie, who led the coup and installed Major Johnny Paul Koroma as military leader, said it would be impossible to strike a deal without rebel leader Foday Sankoh, who remains under effective house arrest in Nigeria.
Koroma has named Sankoh, who was listed on the Freetown delegation, as his number two. "You can't make any peace in Sierra Leone without Foday Sankoh," Gborie said.
The envoys of Sierra Leone's military rulers and their rebel allies, who rallied to the coup, met ministers representing ECOWAS from Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Ghana and Guinea.

Junta spokesman Allieu Kamara said it wanted to publicise what he called the corruption of ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and fraud that helped him to win a 1996 multi-party elections that ended four years of military rule.

The late arrival from Liberia of Ikimi and Ghana's deputy foreign minister, Victor Gbeho, delayed the start of talks. Delegates said the ministers were keen to return to Liberia for Saturday's elections.

Members of the Sierra Leone delegation earlier displayed bitterness towards Nigeria, which commands ECOMOG, an ECOWAS military force in both Liberia and Sierra Leone. They denounced Nigerian belligerence and praised Ghanaian diplomacy.
"We are ready to disarm, but we can't with the Nigerians bombing our country," Gborie said.
Sierra Leone's neighbours decided in Guinea on June 26 to pursue dialogue and economic sanctions to try to persuade the junta to reinstate Kabbah, but they retained a military option.
Nigerian soldiers have clashed with Sierra Leone troops and their rebel allies on several occasions since Nigerian gunboats bombarded the capital in a June 2 show of force.
The junta's foreign minister, Paolo Bangura, is leading the Freetown delegation.
